text_blocks.snippet: Early signs of type 2 diabetes include increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue as the body struggles to process sugar.
snippet_highlighted_words: increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue

list.snippet: Increased thirst and frequent urination: High blood sugar forces your kidneys to work overtime to flush out extra glucose, which pulls fluid from your tissues.
Constant fatigue: Your cells cannot absorb glucose properly for energy, leaving you exhausted even after sleeping.
Blurred vision: High sugar levels can change fluid levels in the lenses of your eyes, making your sight fuzzy.
Slow-healing cuts and sores: Reduced blood flow and high sugar make it harder for wounds, cuts, or bruises to heal.
Frequent infections: Bacteria and yeast thrive on excess sugar, leading to more urinary tract or skin infections.
Tingling or numbness: Nerve damage from high blood sugar can cause a "pins and needles" feeling in your hands or feet.
Dark skin patches: Velvety dark patches (acanthosis nigricans) on the neck or armpits can signal insulin resistance.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more about overall indicators and risk factors on the Mayo Clinic Type 2 Diabetes Overview or review the CDC Diabetes Symptoms Guide.
